gen-gf-sniglet-fs-plein: Rounded and unhurried. Sniglet holds a flat, level line with terminals that stop short of curling, while Plein brings a clear channel into each round letter.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-synonym: Chunky, friendly, a bit commanding. Synonym follows in a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings, so the two sit together like a loud voice and a patient one.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-montserrat: Tilt Neon draws tube-like strokes of constant width, with a splayed c terminal and a large x-height. Montserrat follows in a plain sans with oversized e and a counters, gliding along like wire.
gen-mystery-quest-poppins: Nostalgic, with a bookish tug. Mystery Quest keeps open jaws on its curves and low contrast, while Poppins drops thick-thin flicker entirely and rolls out loose, sturdy lowercase.
gen-audiowide-general-sans: Audiowide sets its glyphs like tiles with wide grout lines, no thick-thin shift anywhere. General Sans answers in a plain sans with an x-height that fills the line, so give it the size that suits reading.
gen-eater-fs-asap: Eater pairs hairline-free thin strokes with weighty stems and wide gaps between letters. Asap steps in as a plain sans with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, which is the steadier half.
gen-gf-funnel-display-archivo: Funnel Display is spaghetti-like, with every stroke the same width. It leads with expressive attitude, while Archivo, a plain sans, brings a commanding x-height and curves that open outward.
gen-gf-gugi-satoshi: Satoshi reads soft and approachable. Its soaring x-height and wide-open e never look squeezed, so paragraphs of plain sans would move easily under Gugi's tall, bold lowercase.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-fs-alpino: Cozy is the mood Alpino carries, with its tall body and curve endings kept well apart. And Love Ya Like A Sister, bold and expressive, has stems like dowels, so its ascenders barely clear the x-height.
gen-gf-turret-road-fs-amulya: Turret Road is bold and commanding, with round forms like open parentheses drawn in a marker-like line. But Amulya, the modern sans-serif here, does its best work with generous gaps in the curves.
